$comment: Shared corpus — quilltap-v5 copies this file verbatim and asserts the same outputs. `cases[].expect` is the WHOLE match object, or null. `mathCases[].expect` is isInsideMathSpan's boolean. Fix the port, not the vectors.

cases.invariant: The ordinary case: a backslash at the start of the run opens on the second query character.
A backslash after whitespace opens; `end` spans the whole query.
CASE IS PRESERVED. `\Phi` is Φ and `\phi` is φ; a port that lowercases here inserts the wrong Greek letter and nothing complains.
Case survives even when no alias has that casing — the ENGINE decides what an unmatched query resolves to, not the trigger.
An opening bracket is a word opening, same as for the emoji profile.
A backslash glued to a letter is somebody else's construct — a Windows path, an escaped literal — not a trigger.
One query character is inert: minQueryLength is 2, so a stray `\a` never flashes a menu.
MARKDOWN ESCAPE. A backslash followed by punctuation is an escape, never a trigger — the query alphabet excludes punctuation entirely.
Same: `\[` is an escaped bracket — and the opener of display math.
Braces are IN the query alphabet (for `\u{1D538}`) but may not START a query, so `\{` stays an escaped brace.
The braced code-point form survives the trigger intact; the engine resolves it arithmetically.
`+` is in the alphabet so the familiar `U+2192` spelling works.
A trailing space CANCELS the trigger. The space commit is a keydown path that probes the text as it read BEFORE the space landed — the menu must not still be open behind it.
Two backslashes running: the second opens no word, so nothing fires rather than guessing which one the writer meant.
One past maxQueryLength abandons the match — pasted text must not hold a menu open.

mathCases.invariant: An unclosed `$$` is display math being typed. Substituting φ here would break the formula.
Single-dollar spans ARE math by the time it matters — normalizeMathDelimiters promotes them before the parser runs.
`\(…\)` is rewritten to `$$` form; CommonMark would otherwise eat the backslash.
THE CASE THAT MATTERS. A dollar followed by a digit is currency, not math, so the menu opens. Quilltap chat is full of prose about money.
A dollar followed by whitespace is not opening a formula either.
A CLOSED display span leaves nothing open behind it.
`$$` is consumed as a unit, so a second span opening after a closed one is still seen.
A single-dollar formula with spaces in it is still a formula.
The overwhelmingly common case costs nothing.
